A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAK research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite appendix expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PASCAL-Context and NYUD-v2 experiments, module and training ablations, teacher-selection studies, and data-size analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original fusion comparisons, teacher-extension studies, classification, depth-probing, and vision-language evaluations in Appendices C and D.

M1.justification: The core TAS, TSAP, MoR, and two-stage training method remains unchanged. Appendix D.4 adds an incremental-teacher procedure: freeze existing TAS/TSAP modules, distill a new adapter branch, then jointly fine-tune the student with all teachers. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Appendix D.6 adds ImageNet-1k classification and LLaVA-based visual question answering on GQA, POPE, and VQAv2, substantially extending v1's dense-prediction coverage. It also reports standalone NYUd depth probing, although the PDFs do not sufficiently describe how its underlying data differ from the retained NYUD-v2 benchmark.

E2.justification: v2 adds direct comparisons against full-teacher fusion systems using addition, concatenation, and MoR (Table 19). The new depth comparison also includes literature-reported MAE and DINO results alongside evaluated and reproduced baselines (Table 27). The original multi-task comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include frozen-backbone classification at resolution 224, depth probing from one or four layers, and LLaVA-1.5 evaluation at resolutions 432 and 512 with frozen TAS/TSAP modules and trained routers (D.6). Sections 2.1 and B.1 also change the stated feature-map resizing target from one-quarter of input resolution to one-quarter of output resolution; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 retains the existing ablations and sensitivity studies while adding full-teacher fusion controls (Table 19), computational-cost analyses (Tables 21–22), SigLIP substitution and incremental-addition tests (Tables 24–25), and one-versus-three-teacher depth probing (Table 27). These test efficiency, teacher dependence, and extension behavior beyond v1's analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 1's retained mean-to-standard-deviation ratio describes variation across tasks, rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: The original benchmark scores are retained, but substantial new results are reported. Table 25 gives MTL gain of -0.45 with added SigLIP versus -0.03 for the original three-teacher configuration. Table 26 reports SAK classification accuracy of 79.1%, versus RADIO's 78.2% and DINOv2's 84.5%. New fusion, cost, depth, and VQA results further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: Equation 3 corrects the adapter's matrix-product order from W_up GELU(W_down R_in) to GELU(R_in W_down) W_up, resolving incompatibility with the stated matrix dimensions. The other formal definitions and losses are retained; no new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about preserving teacher biases, adaptive combination, multi-task performance, efficiency, and flexibility. The headline NYUD-v2 improvement claim is unchanged; the appendix additions provide further evidence and qualifications.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds substantive discussion of heterogeneous routing, teacher-selection constraints, and efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. It proposes explanations for incomplete knowledge transfer, negative transfer, poorer parsing after adding SigLIP, and VQA shortfalls, explicitly expanding the paper's applicability boundaries and limitations.

D1.justification: The original model identifiers, hardware specification, and Table 11 hyperparameters remain unchanged. v2 adds project and repository links, states that code and models are publicly available, explains the provenance of training hyperparameters in B.6, and supplies implementation notes for the additional evaluations.

R1.justification: v2 adds PHI-S and Roth et al. (2024) to the distillation discussion, alongside references supporting new experiments, including DFN, MAE, Binsformer, and LLaVA. The central positioning relative to RADIO, Theia, and prior multi-task learning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The existing main narrative is largely preserved, with limited wording and cross-reference edits. v2 adds acknowledgments, ethics and reproducibility statements, and an appendix roadmap. Inserting Additional Discussions as Appendix D moves the existing related-work and qualitative appendices to E and F.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial tabular presentation for fusion controls, computational costs, teacher selection, and additional tasks: Table 19 and Tables 21–28. Existing appendix tables and figures are redistributed; v1 Tables 19 and 20 become v2 Tables 20 and 29. All eleven original figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct full-teacher fusion controls and quantified module computation costs; v2 supplies both and tests teacher extension and broader applications. Reporting parsing and VQA shortcomings also makes the method's limits clearer. These additions substantially strengthen evaluation of the existing efficiency and flexibility claims, while new code/model access information improves reproducibility. Run-level uncertainty remains unreported.
